title: B-ALL Cytomorphology and Diagnostic Criteria
text: B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) is a neoplasm of precursor cells committed to the B-cell lineage. In bone marrow aspirates, lymphoblasts are typically small to medium-sized with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic (N:C) ratios, finely dispersed or condensed nuclear chromatin, inconspicuous or absent nucleoli, and scant, agranular, light blue to basophilic cytoplasm. Occasional cytoplasmic vacuolization may occur. The diagnosis of acute lymphoblastic leukemia requires >=20% lymphoblasts in the bone marrow or peripheral blood according to classical WHO criteria, although in pediatric settings the presence of clonal B-cell precursors with clinical features warrants full genetic and flow cytometric workup even at lower percentages. B-ALL accounts for approximately 80-85% of pediatric acute leukemias.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: WHO standard blast cutoff in bone marrow aspirate

title: T-ALL Cytomorphology and Differential Characteristics
text: T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (T-ALL) comprises approximately 15% of pediatric acute leukemias. Morphologically, T-lymphoblasts often exhibit greater pleomorphism and size variation compared to B-ALL. Blasts range from medium to large with moderately high N:C ratios, irregular nuclear contours, indented or convoluted nuclei, dispersed chromatin, and one or two distinct nucleoli. Cytoplasm is typically scant to moderate, mildly basophilic, and usually agranular, though occasional azurophilic granules can rarely be present. Mediastinal (thymic) mass and marked leukocytosis are frequent clinical correlates. Lineage assignment requires cytoplasmic CD3 expression by flow cytometry or immunohistochemistry.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Standard acute lymphoblastic leukemia threshold

title: Burkitt Leukemia Cytomorphological Triad and Starry-Sky Pattern
text: Burkitt leukemia (formerly FAB L3 ALL) represents the leukemic manifestation of Burkitt lymphoma. The cytomorphological hallmark consists of medium-sized, round to oval, monomorphic blast cells with intensely basophilic, royal blue cytoplasm containing prominent, round lipid vacuoles that often overlay the nucleus. Nuclei are round or oval with moderately coarse, clumped chromatin and 2 to 5 distinct basophilic nucleoli. Bone marrow exhibits a high mitotic index and widespread apoptosis with 'starry-sky' macrophage phagocytosis of apoptotic debris. Driven by MYC gene translocations (primarily t(8;14)(q24;q32)), Burkitt leukemia represents an oncologic emergency requiring rapid high-intensity pulse chemotherapy rather than standard ALL protocols.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Bone marrow involvement by mature B-cell Burkitt blasts

specific_entity: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) General Diagnostic Criteria
title: AML Definition and Blast Cutoffs in Pediatric Patients
text: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) is defined as a clonal expansion of myeloid blasts in the bone marrow, blood, or other tissue. The standard diagnostic threshold is >=20% myeloid blasts among nucleated marrow cells. However, both the WHO 5th edition and ICC 2022 recognize that patients harboring specific recurrent genetic abnormalities—notably t(8;21)(q22;q22.1) RUNX1::RUNX1T1, inv(16)(p13.1q22) CBFB::MYH11, and PML::RARA—are diagnosed with AML regardless of the blast percentage. Myeloid blasts are characteristically larger than lymphoblasts, with round to oval nuclei, delicate reticular chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and moderate amounts of gray-blue cytoplasm often containing fine azurophilic granules.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Standard blast cutoff, waived for defining genetic abnormalities like PML::RARA, RUNX1::RUNX1T1

specific_entity: AML with Recurrent Cytogenetics & APL t(15;17)
title: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL) and Distinct Morphological Clues
text: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL) with PML::RARA is characterized by abnormal hypergranular promyelocytes with kidney-shaped or bilobed nuclei and dense, coarse azurophilic granules covering the cytoplasm and obscuring nuclear borders. Multiple Auer rods arranged in bundles ('faggot cells') are pathognomonic. In microgranular variant APL, granules are submicroscopic, with distinct butterfly-shaped or reniform folded nuclei. Prompt recognition is critical because APL frequently presents with severe disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC); immediate administration of all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) and arsenic trioxide (ATO) is lifesaving before molecular confirmation. Auer rods in myeloblasts generally indicate myeloid lineage commitment.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Presence of PML::RARA defines APL regardless of blast count

title: AML with Maturation (FAB M2) and Acute Myelomonocytic Leukemia (FAB M4)
text: In AML with maturation, bone marrow blasts constitute >=20% of non-erythroid cells, and maturing granulocytes (promyelocytes, myelocytes, metamyelocytes, neutrophils) exceed 10%. Neutrophilic maturation often displays dysplastic features including hypogranulation and pseudo-Pelger-Huet nuclear hypolobulation. In Acute Myelomonocytic Leukemia (AMMoL), bone marrow exhibits both myeloblasts and monoblasts/promonocytes, each comprising >=20% of the differential, with peripheral monocytosis >=1.0x10^9/L. Monoblasts are large with abundant weakly basophilic cytoplasm, round nuclei, delicate chromatin, and large vesicular nucleoli.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts >=20% with evidence of myeloid maturation

title: CML Chronic Phase Cytomorphology and the 'Myelocyte Bulge'
text: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML), BCR::ABL1-positive, is a myeloproliferative neoplasm originating in a pluripotent hematopoietic stem cell. In the chronic phase (CML-CP), bone marrow aspirates are markedly hypercellular with extreme granulocytic hyperplasia and a high myeloid-to-erythroid (M:E) ratio (frequently 10:1 to 30:1). A diagnostic cytomorphological hallmark is the 'myelocyte bulge', where intermediate granulocytic precursors (myelocytes and metamyelocytes) outnumber more immature promyelocytes and myeloblasts. Blast percentage remains strictly <10% in marrow and peripheral blood. Absolute basophilia and eosinophilia are consistently present. Megakaryocytes are typically increased in number but smaller than normal with hypolobated nuclei ('dwarf megakaryocytes').

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts must be strictly <10% to meet Chronic Phase criteria

title: CML Progression: Accelerated Phase vs. Blast Phase Criteria
text: Progression of CML signifies treatment failure or resistance. Under WHO 5th edition and ICC criteria: Accelerated Phase (CML-AP) is defined by 10-19% blasts in bone marrow or blood, persistent basophilia >=20%, persistent thrombocytopenia (<100x10^9/L) or thrombocytosis (>1000x10^9/L) unresponsive to therapy, and additional clonal cytogenetic abnormalities. Blast Phase (CML-BP) is defined by >=20% blasts in the bone marrow or peripheral blood, or extramedullary blastic proliferation. Notably, in pediatric CML-BP, approximately 70% of blast transformations are myeloid in phenotype, while 30% are lymphoid (B-ALL phenotype), requiring distinct lineage-targeted therapeutic strategies alongside tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).

blast_threshold_rule.condition: >=20% blasts defines CML Blast Phase

specific_entity: Haematogones vs. Leukemic Lymphoblasts in Children
title: Distinguishing Benign Haematogones from Malignant B-ALL Blasts
text: A critical diagnostic pitfall in pediatric bone marrow cytomorphology is distinguishing benign B-cell precursor hyperplasia (haematogones) from residual or emerging B-ALL lymphoblasts. Haematogones can normally constitute up to 5-15% (and occasionally >20% following viral infections, immune reconstitution, or chemotherapy) of bone marrow nucleated cells in young children. Cytomorphologically, haematogones exhibit a continuous spectrum of maturation from small immature cells (scant cytoplasm, round condensed nuclei, indistinct nucleoli) to intermediate and mature lymphocytes. In contrast, B-ALL lymphoblasts display a sharp 'maturational arrest' presenting as a monomorphic clone with abnormal chromatin, irregular nuclear clefts, and distinct immunophenotypic aberrancies (e.g., aberrant CD10/CD20/CD34 co-expression and CD58 upregulation).

blast_threshold_rule.warning: Haematogones must not be misclassified as leukemic blasts without flow cytometric confirmation

specific_entity: Reactive Bone Marrow and Non-Malignant Marrow Responses
title: Reactive Granulocytic Hyperplasia, Infection, and Normal Pediatric Cellularity
text: Normal pediatric bone marrow cellularity is age-dependent, typically approximating 80-90% in young infants, declining to 60-70% in older children. In systemic infections or severe inflammatory stress, reactive granulocytic hyperplasia may produce marked myeloid expansion and high M:E ratios that superficially resemble CML. However, reactive leukemoid responses demonstrate normal or elevated leukocyte alkaline phosphatase (LAP) scores, toxic granulation, Dohle bodies, cytoplasmic vacuolation in mature neutrophils, and lack the severe 'myelocyte bulge' and prominent basophilia typical of CML. Blasts remain normal (<5%). Reactive erythroid hyperplasia occurs in hemolytic conditions, while transient erythroblastopenia of childhood (TEC) shows temporary erythroid hypoplasia with spontaneous recovery.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Normal and reactive bone marrow maintains <5% blasts

title: Mixed Phenotype Acute Leukemia Diagnostic Lineage Criteria
text: Mixed Phenotype Acute Leukemia (MPAL) is a rare acute leukemia comprising approximately 2-3% of pediatric leukemias where the blast population meets definitive lineage criteria for more than one hematopoietic lineage (either a single biphenotypic population or two distinct blast populations, bilineal). Criteria require strong lineage assignment: for B-lineage, strong CD19 with bright expression of at least one other B-marker (CD79a, cCD22, CD10); for T-lineage, bright cytoplasmic or surface CD3; for Myeloid, myeloperoxidase (MPO) positivity or unequivocal monocytic differentiation (at least 2 markers: NSE, CD11c, CD14, CD64). Morphology alone cannot reliably establish MPAL, making comprehensive multiparameter flow cytometry essential.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: >=20% acute leukemia blasts with dual or multiple lineage commitment

specific_entity: Monolayer ROI Sampling vs. Clinical Aspirate Differentials
title: Scientific Limitation: Annotated-Cell Fraction vs. Whole-Slide Clinical Blast Differential
text: In digital pathology datasets of whole slide bone marrow aspirates (such as BoneMarrowWSI-PediatricLeukemia), annotations are typically collected from pre-selected high-power monolayer fields optimized for cell morphology assessment. Consequently, the 'annotated-cell blast fraction' calculated from consensus boxes represents the proportion of blasts within these specific sampling regions, NOT an exhaustive 500-cell clinical aspirate differential count from the entire slide. Furthermore, spicules, macroscopic tissue particles, and technically damaged cells are excluded from single-cell analysis. Decision support systems must transparently distinguish between local monolayer blast densities and true whole-slide clinical differentials.

blast_threshold_rule.warning: Annotated blast fraction is a localized computational metric and cannot substitute for an exhaustive clinical differential

title: MDS-EB1 Blast Percentage and Dysplasia Criteria
text: Myelodysplastic Syndrome with Excess Blasts-1 (MDS-EB1) is defined by 5-9% blasts in bone marrow or 2-4% blasts in peripheral blood, with dysplasia in one or more myeloid lineages. Dyserythropoiesis includes megaloblastic changes, nuclear budding, karyorrhexis, and multinuclearity. Dysgranulopoiesis features hypogranular or agranular neutrophils, pseudo-Pelger-Huet anomaly (bilobed nuclei), and abnormal nuclear segmentation. Dysmegakaryopoiesis shows hypolobated ('peanut') or multilobated nuclei and micromegakaryocytes. Auer rods are absent in MDS-EB1. Progression to AML occurs in 25-30% of cases within 2 years.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: 5-9% marrow blasts or 2-4% peripheral blasts

title: MDS-EB2 High Blast Count and Auer Rod Presence
text: MDS with Excess Blasts-2 (MDS-EB2) is characterized by 10-19% blasts in bone marrow or 5-19% blasts in peripheral blood, with multilineage dysplasia. Auer rods may be present in <20% blasts, distinguishing this from AML. MDS-EB2 represents high-risk disease with 40-50% progression to AML within 1 year. Morphologically indistinguishable from low-blast AML, the 20% blast cutoff remains arbitrary but clinically validated. Cytogenetics strongly influence prognosis: complex karyotype (>=3 abnormalities), monosomy 7, or del(7q) confer very poor outcomes requiring early allogeneic transplant consideration.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: 10-19% marrow blasts or 5-19% peripheral blasts

title: MDS with del(5q) - Hypolobated Megakaryocytes and Anemia
text: MDS with isolated del(5q) is characterized by anemia (often macrocytic), normal or elevated platelet count, <5% marrow blasts, and del(5q) as sole cytogenetic abnormality. Morphologically distinctive: bone marrow shows hypolobated megakaryocytes with separated nuclear lobes ('peanut-shaped' nuclei), erythroid hyperplasia with dyserythropoiesis, and variable granulocytic hypoplasia. This subtype responds favorably to lenalidomide therapy, achieving transfusion independence in ~70% of patients. Presence of TP53 mutations or additional cytogenetic abnormalities abrogates favorable prognosis.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts <5% with isolated del(5q) cytogenetics

specific_entity: MDS with Ring Sideroblasts and SF3B1 Mutation
title: MDS-RS with SF3B1 - Ring Sideroblasts and Iron Overload
text: MDS with ring sideroblasts (MDS-RS) is defined by >=15% ring sideroblasts (or >=5% if SF3B1 mutation present) with <5% marrow blasts. Ring sideroblasts are erythroid precursors with >=5 iron-laden mitochondria forming a perinuclear ring, visible on Prussian blue (Perls) iron stain. SF3B1 mutations occur in >80% of MDS-RS cases, involving RNA splicing machinery. Morphology shows erythroid hyperplasia with dyserythropoiesis, variable dysgranulopoiesis, and normal or hypolobated megakaryocytes. Prognosis is favorable with median survival >5 years, though iron overload from transfusion dependence requires chelation therapy.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts <5% with >=15% ring sideroblasts (or >=5% with SF3B1 mutation)

title: MDS-MLD Pancytopenia and Multilineage Morphological Abnormalities
text: MDS with multilineage dysplasia (MDS-MLD) presents with cytopenia in 2-3 lineages, <5% marrow blasts, <1x10^9/L monocytes, and no Auer rods. Dysplasia must involve >=10% of cells in 2 or more myeloid lineages. Common dyserythropoietic features: megaloblastoid maturation, nuclear budding, karyorrhexis, multinuclearity, cytoplasmic vacuolation, and ring sideroblasts. Dysgranulopoiesis: hypogranular neutrophils, pseudo-Pelger-Huet anomaly, ring-shaped nuclei. Dysmegakaryopoiesis: micromegakaryocytes, hypolobated nuclei, multiple separated nuclear lobes. MDS-MLD has intermediate prognosis with median survival 2-3 years.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts <5% with dysplasia in >=2 lineages

title: Polycythemia Vera Diagnostic Criteria and JAK2 V617F
text: Polycythemia Vera (PV) is a JAK2-mutated myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by erythrocytosis, often with leukocytosis and thrombocytosis. Bone marrow shows panmyelosis with trilineage proliferation, increased cellularity (age-adjusted), and clustered pleomorphic megakaryocytes. Erythroid islands are prominent. Diagnosis requires: (1) elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit (>16.5 g/dL Hb male, >16.0 female; OR Hct >49% male, >48% female), (2) bone marrow panmyelosis with pleomorphic megakaryocytes, and (3) JAK2 V617F or JAK2 exon 12 mutation. Reticulin fibrosis grade 0-1 initially, though MF-3 fibrosis may develop ('spent phase'). Low erythropoietin levels support diagnosis.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts <2% in chronic phase PV

title: Essential Thrombocythemia Megakaryocyte Morphology and Mutations
text: Essential Thrombocythemia (ET) is characterized by sustained thrombocytosis (platelets >=450x10^9/L), bone marrow proliferation of enlarged mature megakaryocytes with hyperlobulated 'staghorn' nuclei, and absence of significant reticulin fibrosis (grade 0-1). Diagnosis requires exclusion of CML (BCR::ABL1 negative), PV (normal Hb/Hct), PMF, and reactive causes. Driver mutations: JAK2 V617F (50-60%), CALR exon 9 (20-25%), or MPL exon 10 (3-5%). Triple-negative ET (15%) exists. Morphologically, megakaryocytes display deep nuclear lobulation, loose clusters, and normal M:E ratio. Thrombotic risk is highest with JAK2 mutations, while CALR-mutated ET has better prognosis.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts <2% in chronic phase ET

title: Primary Myelofibrosis Reticulin Grade and Dacrocytes
text: Primary Myelofibrosis (PMF) presents with bone marrow fibrosis (reticulin grade 2-3 or collagen grade 1-3), leukoerythroblastosis, dacrocytes (teardrop cells) in peripheral smear, splenomegaly, and anemia. Pre-fibrotic/early PMF shows hypercellular marrow with megakaryocyte proliferation and atypia (cloud-like, ballooned nuclei) without significant fibrosis. Overt PMF exhibits dense reticulin/collagen fibrosis, dilated sinusoids, intrasinusoidal hematopoiesis, and 'dry tap' aspirates requiring trephine biopsy. Driver mutations mirror ET (JAK2, CALR, MPL). High-molecular-risk mutations (ASXL1, EZH2, SRSF2, IDH1/2) worsen prognosis. Blasts <10% distinguish PMF from accelerated/blast phase.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts <10% in chronic phase PMF; >=10% indicates acceleration

title: CNL with CSF3R T618I Mutation
text: Chronic Neutrophilic Leukemia (CNL) is a rare BCR::ABL1-negative MPN characterized by sustained neutrophilia (>=25x10^9/L), bone marrow hypercellularity with neutrophilic granulocytosis and <10% myeloblasts, hepatosplenomegaly, and CSF3R T618I (or other activating CSF3R) mutations in >80% of cases. Morphologically, peripheral blood shows segmented neutrophils and band forms with <10% immature granulocytes and <10% metamyelocytes. Absence of monocytosis (<1x10^9/L), dysplasia, and BCR::ABL1/PDGFRA/PDGFRB rearrangements distinguish CNL from CML, atypical CML, and CEL. Prognosis is poor with median survival 2-3 years; transformation to AML occurs in 20%.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts <10% with neutrophilia >=25x10^9/L

title: CEL Eosinophilia and Clonal Markers
text: Chronic Eosinophilic Leukemia, Not Otherwise Specified (CEL-NOS) is characterized by sustained eosinophilia (>=1.5x10^9/L), clonal cytogenetic or molecular abnormality, <20% marrow blasts, and exclusion of PDGFRA/PDGFRB/FGFR1/PCM1-JAK2 rearrangements. Bone marrow shows eosinophilic proliferation with various maturation stages; eosinophils may display morphological abnormalities (hypogranulation, cytoplasmic vacuolation, nuclear hypolobation). Blasts may be increased (2-19%) with myeloid or eosinophil-lineage features. CEL must be distinguished from reactive hypereosinophilia (parasitic, allergic, drug-induced) and hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES, which lacks clonality markers). Organ damage (cardiac, pulmonary, neurologic) from eosinophil-derived cytotoxic proteins is common.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts <20% with clonal eosinophilia

title: TAM in Down Syndrome Neonates
text: Transient Abnormal Myelopoiesis (TAM), also termed transient myeloproliferative disorder, occurs in 10% of neonates with Down syndrome (trisomy 21) or mosaic trisomy 21. Characterized by clonal proliferation of megakaryoblasts with acquired GATA1 mutations, TAM typically presents in the first week of life with hepatosplenomegaly, hydrops, or circulating blast cells. Morphologically, peripheral blood shows 10-30% (sometimes >50%) circulating megakaryoblasts or basophilic blasts with cytoplasmic blebs. Bone marrow may show extensive fibrosis. TAM spontaneously resolves within 3 months in 80% of cases, but 20-30% of survivors develop myeloid leukemia of Down syndrome (ML-DS) within 4 years, also harboring GATA1 mutations.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: >=10% circulating blasts in Down syndrome neonate

title: ML-DS and GATA1 Mutation Requirement
text: Myeloid Leukemia associated with Down Syndrome (ML-DS) occurs in children with constitutional trisomy 21 or mosaic trisomy 21, typically aged 1-4 years. Morphologically, ML-DS exhibits megakaryoblastic (60%) or myeloid differentiation with dysplastic features, often preceded by a myelodysplastic phase. Blasts are usually >=20% but diagnosis can be made with <20% if GATA1 mutation confirmed. GATA1 mutations are mandatory for ML-DS diagnosis. Compared to non-Down syndrome AMKL, ML-DS has excellent prognosis with 5-year OS >85% using reduced-intensity chemotherapy; allogeneic transplant is rarely required. Bone marrow often shows marked fibrosis and dysmegakaryopoiesis.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: >=20% blasts (or <20% with GATA1 mutation) in trisomy 21

title: LCH Marrow Infiltration and BRAF V600E
text: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH) is a clonal neoplastic proliferation of dendritic cells with Langerhans cell phenotype. Bone marrow involvement occurs in 10-15% of multisystem LCH cases and portends poor prognosis (risk organ involvement). Morphologically, LCH cells are medium to large with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, kidney-shaped or folded nuclei, fine chromatin, and indistinct nucleoli. Characteristic longitudinal nuclear grooves ('coffee-bean' nuclei) may be visible. Admixed eosinophils, lymphocytes, and multinucleated giant cells create a mixed inflammatory background. Immunophenotype: CD1a+, CD207 (langerin)+, S100+. BRAF V600E mutations occur in 50-60% of LCH; MEK inhibitors show therapeutic efficacy in refractory disease.

blast_threshold_rule.warning: LCH cells mimic histiocytes, not blasts; diagnosis requires CD1a/CD207 positivity

title: HLH Bone Marrow Hemophagocytosis
text: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome, primary (genetic) or secondary (infection, malignancy, autoimmune). Bone marrow findings include prominent hemophagocytosis: activated macrophages engulfing erythrocytes, leukocytes, platelets, or their precursors. Hemophagocytes are large histiocytes with abundant cytoplasm containing ingested cells. Diagnostic criteria (HLH-2004): fever, splenomegaly, cytopenia (>=2 lineages), hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, elevated ferritin (>=500 μg/L, often >10,000), elevated sCD25, decreased NK cell activity, and/or hemophagocytosis in marrow/spleen/lymph nodes. Genetic HLH involves PRF1, UNC13D, STX11, STXBP2 mutations. Treatment: HLH-94/2004 protocol with etoposide and dexamethasone.

blast_threshold_rule.warning: HLH macrophages are not blasts; distinguish from malignant histiocytosis

title: Distinguishing Severe Aplastic Anemia from Hypoplastic MDS
text: Severe Aplastic Anemia (SAA) presents with pancytopenia (ANC <0.5x10^9/L, platelets <20x10^9/L, reticulocytes <20x10^9/L) and markedly hypocellular bone marrow (<25% cellularity, or <50% with <30% hematopoietic cells). Morphologically, marrow shows fatty replacement with scattered residual lymphocytes, plasma cells, and mast cells, but NO dysplasia and NO increased blasts. Hypoplastic MDS also shows hypocellularity but exhibits dysplastic morphology in >=10% of cells in one or more lineages, abnormal cytogenetics (monosomy 7, trisomy 8, del(20q)), and/or increased blasts. Flow cytometry showing absent or reduced CD34+ cells favors AA, while increased CD34+ blasts with aberrant phenotypes suggests hypoplastic MDS. PNH clone detection (CD55/CD59 deficiency) supports AA.

blast_threshold_rule.condition: Blasts <2% in aplastic anemia; >=5% suggests hypoplastic MDS
